writeup.p: Server-to-client broadcast of a named sound at a fixed-point position. The server computes a delivery radius of 16 blocks, scaled by volume when volume exceeds 1.0, and fans the packet out through ConfigurationManager.sendToAllNear. The client handler converts the x8 fixed-point ints back to doubles and hands the call to World.playSound. Because the sound name is an arbitrary server-controlled string, the field is both a gameplay input and a data-injection surface for anything downstream that logs or parses it.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleSoundEffect does PacketThreadUtil.func_180031_a (main-thread marshalling) then World.playSound(name, x/8, y/8, z/8, volume, pitch/63, false). The pitch arrives as an unsigned byte with 63 meaning normal pitch; the client divides by 63.0F. Server side the packet is created by WorldManager.playSound and playSoundAtEntity, and by /playsound (CommandPlaySound), which converts double coordinates to the x8 int encoding. Netty reads the name with a 256-char cap via readStringFromBuffer(256).

Only two real handlers exist across the 8 clients, and neither is a sound-ESP. Rise 5.99's Disabler, in its HypixelSlime mode, cancels the mob.slime.big sound to strip the Hypixel double-jump slime indicator. Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 route the packet through LoggerRCECheck, a security feature that matches the sound name against a ${...} pattern to catch Log4j RCE attempts (CVE-2021-44228): sound names are logged by the client logger, so a crafted name is an injection vector. No client in the corpus tracks sounds for ESP purposes.

The sound name string is the interesting field. It passes through String formatting and logger calls on both ends, which is exactly the Log4j RCE chain that LoggerRCECheck defends. Volume has no clamp on the wire, so a malicious server can send volume values far above 1.0 and inflate the client-side audio range beyond the 16-block visibility radius. The pitch byte is unsigned, so values above 127 encode negative pitches when interpreted as signed, a quirk modules rarely bother with.

overview: A pure world-effect broadcast: named sound, x8 fixed-point position, volume, pitch byte. The 8 clients barely touch it. The only module-grade hit is Rise 5.99's Disabler cancelling the Hypixel slime jump sound; Rise 6.x handles it as a Log4j RCE scan surface rather than as audio.
server_handling: WorldManager.playSound sends to all players within 16 blocks, or 16*volume when volume > 1.0F, on the same dimension. CommandPlaySound builds the packet from parsed coordinates (x*8, y*8, z*8) and clamps pitch to 0..255 before writing. The client handler marshals to the main thread, then plays the sound with pitch = raw byte / 63.0F. No server-side rate limit exists; sound spam is only bounded by the 256-char name cap and the per-packet cost.
protocol_notes: Encoding order: String name (max 256), int x*8, int y*8, int z*8, float volume, unsigned byte pitch. The y field is initialized to Integer.MAX_VALUE in the no-arg constructor as a sentinel for the client-side y-clamping fallback (field_149218_c). In 1.8.9 MCP this packet predates the generic Packet<T> signature, so it implements raw Packet and does a double dispatch through processPacket.
anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats do not flag sound packets; they are cosmetic. The abuse surface is the name string, and the relevant defense is client-side: Rise's LoggerRCECheck pattern-matches ${...} in the name to block Log4j RCE payloads that would otherwise execute through the client's logging pipeline. Because the packet is clientbound and server-trusted, there is no bypass trade-off: a compromised server can always send it, so the check is a pure filter.

modules.name: Disabler (HypixelSlime sound cancel)
modules.purpose: Cancel the mob.slime.big sound on Hypixel so the double-jump slime indicator never plays.
modules.how_it_works: In the HypixelSlime mode branch of the packet receive handler, every S29 is type-checked; if the sound name equals mob.slime.big the event is cancelled. The same mode also cancels SLIME-type S2APacketParticles and S1FPacketSetExperience, so the whole Hypixel double-jump visual cluster is stripped together.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Zero detection risk: cancelling a clientbound sound is invisible to the server. The only observable effect is the missing slime sound on the local client.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 do not carry this mode; their only S29 reference is LoggerRCECheck in the security pipeline.

modules.name: LoggerRCECheck (security)
modules.purpose: Block Log4j RCE payloads carried in the sound name string.
modules.how_it_works: A SecurityFeature registered in Rise's packet security chain. On every packet it checks the S29 sound name against the regex .*\$\{[^}]*}.*. A match returns true, which drops the packet before it reaches the game logic or any logging path. The same check also guards S02PacketChat text. It is a security component, not a toggleable user module.
modules.vanilla_hook: Security pipeline handle(Packet) invoked per received packet.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Not anti-cheat related. It defends the client against malicious servers; the cost is a regex match on every S29 and S02, which is negligible at server tick rates.
modules.variations: Identical file in Rise 6.1.30 (com/alan/clients/security/impl/LoggerRCECheck.java). The packet class is also listed in Rise's NetworkAPI script bridge, which exposes it to JavaScript scripts but adds no game logic.

general_hooks: Both handlers sit on the packet receive path: Rise 5.99 uses PacketReceiveEvent, Rise 6.x uses the security chain that pre-filters every inbound packet before module dispatch.
client_variations: Rise 5.99 mutates/cancels via event.setCancelled on PacketReceiveEvent. Rise 6.1.30/6.2.4 moved packet filtering into the SecurityFeature abstraction, which returns a boolean from handle(Packet) and lets the pipeline decide whether to drop.
